mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 8% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 8% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) when UNRATE exceeds 8% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which lowers earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when INDPRO declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% signals a dual tightening in monetary and inflationary conditions, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 2% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in housing starts (HOUST) above a 12-month moving average by more than 10% indicates a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises by >10% above its 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST rises by more than 10% above its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month is a statistical artifact indicating data revision noise rather than economic signal; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days should be indistinguishable from random walk (no directional bias).
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns show a statistically significant deviation (p < 0.05) from a random walk when PAYEMS and UNRATE move in opposite directions in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 15% suggests households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average by more than 15%.
